summary: Otto Rosenberg (1888–1919) worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Saint Petersburg under Theodore Stcherbatsky and Sergey Oldenburg, in Bonn, and under Rudolf Lange, later holding posts at Saint Petersburg from 1911 to 1919.

Otto Stein (1893–1942) was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Prague, studying under doctoral supervisors Moriz Winternitz and Heinrich Swoboda. In 1929, he joined the Research Section of the Oriental Institute of the Czech Academy.

Otto Strauss (1881–1940) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Munich, Berlin, and Kiel, completing his doctorate under Hermann Oldenberg and Paul Deussen. He held professorships at Calcutta (1913–1920), Kiel (1920), and Breslau (1928–1935).

Otto von Böhtlingk (1815–1904) was an Indologist and linguist who studied in Saint Petersburg, Berlin under Franz Bopp, and Bonn under Christian Lassen. He served at the Imperial Academy of Sciences (1842–1868) and the University of Jena (~1868–1885).
Owen Flanagan (born 1949) specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fordham University and Boston University, and became Professor of Philosophy at Duke University around 1996.

P. B. Annangaracharya (1891–1982) was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar who studied under Asuri Ramanujacharya. He is attested as Head Pandit at Sanskrit Pathashala, Vadtal, in 1954.
P. B. Meegaskumbura is an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar attested as a professor at the University of Peradeniya in 1991 and 2010.
P. H. Joshi is an Indologist who served as a Research Officer at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, attested from 1976 to 1988, and was further attested there in 2002.
P. K. Mukhopadhyay is a philosophy and Indology scholar who served as Professor of Philosophy at Jadavpur University and as a National Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research in 2009.

P. N. Pattabhirama Sastri (1908–1992) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under A. Chinnaswami Sastri. He worked at Banaras Hindu University around 1941 and served as Reader in Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (~1948–1966).

P. P. Subrahmanya Sastri was an Indologist who studied at the University of Madras and the University of Oxford. He served as Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library and Head of Sanskrit at Presidency College, Chennai, attested between 1937 and 1944.

P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri (1890–1978) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Madras. He served at Bishop Heber College, Rajah's College (1932–1942), and as Sanskrit department head at Annamalai University (1942–1947).
P. Swaminathan is an Indologist who completed an M.Litt. at the University of Madras under V. Raghavan in 1956. He served as Lecturer in Sanskrit at Rashtriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha, attested in 1965.
P. T. Narasimhachar (1905–1998) was an Indology scholar who studied under Mysore Hiriyanna at Maharaja's College, Mysore, around 1923 to 1926.
P. V. Ramanujaswami was an Indologist attested as Director of the Sri Venkateswara Oriental Research Institute in 1944 and 1954.

Padma Subrahmanyam (born 1943) is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. She studied at Ethiraj College, Stella Maris College, and Annamalai University (~1975–1979) under research supervisor T. N. Ramachandran.

Padmanabh S. Jaini (1923–2021) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sukhlal Sanghvi. He served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley, attested from 1977 and later as Professor Emeritus.
Padmaprasad Upadhyaya Bhattarai was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Vamacharana Bhattacharya. He held a post at Rajkiya Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya, Kathmandu, attested in 1957.

Pahalawattage Don Premasiri (born 1941) specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned degrees at Peradeniya, Cambridge, and Hawaiʻi (PhD under Kalupahana and Deutsch), and served long-term as professor and department head at the University of Peradeniya (1968–2004).

Palmira Brummett (born 1950) is a historian who earned degrees from the University of Chicago and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. She served at the University of Tennessee (~1989–2011) and as a visiting professor at Brown University (2011–2016).
